questions.question: Explain two ways in which the German Constitution was undemocratic. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: The Chancellor was responsible only to the Kaiser, not the elected Reichstag, meaning parliament could not hold the government to account. The Prussian three-class voting system gave the wealthy minority control over elections, and Prussia had 17 of 58 Bundesrat votes, enough to veto any constitutional change.

questions.question: How far did Prussian influence dominate Imperial Germany? Explain your answer. (12 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Prussia dominated through: the Kaiser was always the King of Prussia; Prussia had 17 of 58 Bundesrat votes (enough to block changes); the Junker class controlled the army and civil service; the three-class franchise in Prussia was deeply undemocratic. questions.question: What was Weltpolitik and why did Wilhelm II pursue it instead of Bismarck's Realpolitik? (8 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Weltpolitik was Wilhelm's policy of making Germany a world power through colonial expansion and naval build-up. He pursued it because he believed Germany deserved a "place in the sun," wanted to challenge British naval supremacy, and saw Bismarck's careful diplomacy as too cautious. Bismarck's Realpolitik had focused on peace and isolation of France; Wilhelm wanted global prestige.

tests.description: Short-answer practice on Kaiser Wilhelm and Germany

questions.question: Explain why the Navy Laws were significant for Germany's foreign relations. (8 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: The Navy Laws provoked a naval arms race with Britain, pushing Britain towards the Triple Entente with France and Russia (1907). They created financial strain, requiring higher taxes and diverting funds from social reform. The Morocco Crises (1905, 1911) showed Germany's aggressive diplomacy isolated it further. The Laws made Britain see Germany as a direct threat rather than a potential ally.

questions.question: "The SPD was the biggest threat to the Kaiser's regime." How far do you agree? (16 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: The SPD was a significant threat as the largest Reichstag party by 1912 (110 seats), representing working-class demands for reform. However, the constitution limited the SPD's effectiveness: the Chancellor was appointed by the Kaiser, the Bundesrat could veto laws, and the army remained loyal to the Kaiser.
